caption: Figure 1: Replaced token detection pre-training consistently outperforms masked language model pre-training given the same compute budget. The left figure is a zoomed-in view of the dashed box.

Figure 2: An overview of replaced token detection. The generator can be any model that produces an output distribution over tokens, but we usually use a small masked language model that is trained jointly with the discriminator.
Although the models are structured like in a GAN, we train the generator with maximum likelihood rather than adversarially due to the difficulty of applying GANs to text.
After pre-training, we throw out the generator and only fine-tune the discriminator (the ELECTRA model) on downstream tasks.

Figure 3: Left : GLUE scores for different generator/discriminator sizes (number of hidden units). Interestingly, having a generator smaller than the discriminator improves results. Right : Comparison of different training algorithms. As our focus is on efficiency, the x-axis shows FLOPs rather than train steps (e.g., ELECTRA is trained for fewer steps than BERT because it includes the generator).
